topic: Should You Quit Your Job for AI?
title: Should You Quit Your Job for AI? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council debates whether you should leave your stable career to chase opportunities in artificial intelligence.

#CareerAdvice #AI #QuitYourJob #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: Quitting a stable job for AI is reckless. Most people don't understand the technology well enough to compete with those who've been in it for years.
But waiting means falling behind. AI is moving faster than any industry shift we've ever seen. The window to transition is now, not in five years.
You don't have to quit to start. Build AI skills on the side. Ship a project. Get traction. Then make the leap with evidence, not hope.
I quit my marketing job six months ago to go all in on AI automation. I'm already making more than my old salary. The risk was worth it.
Survivorship bias. For every Hoshi, there are a hundred people who quit and burned through savings. The smart move is strategic, not impulsive.

topic: Is a College Degree Worthless Now?
title: Is a College Degree Worthless in 2026? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council examines whether traditional degrees still matter in the age of AI and self-taught skills.

#College #Education #CareerAdvice #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: I've interviewed hundreds of candidates. The best ones taught themselves online. The degree told me nothing about their actual ability.
That works for tech. But try becoming a doctor, a lawyer, or an engineer without a degree. Credentials matter in regulated fields.
The degree isn't worthless. The debt is the problem. If college were free, nobody would be having this conversation.
Google, Apple, and Tesla all dropped degree requirements. When the biggest companies stop caring, the signal is clear.
College gives you a network, not just knowledge. The people you meet at twenty-two open doors at thirty-five. You can't replicate that on YouTube.

topic: Should You Learn to Code in 2026?
title: Should You Learn to Code in 2026? | The Global Council
description:
With AI writing code now, is learning to program still worth the investment of time and effort?

#LearnToCode #Programming #AI #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: AI writes code now. Learning syntax is like learning to shoe horses in the age of cars. Learn to direct AI instead.
Hard disagree. Understanding code means understanding logic. AI is a tool, not a replacement for thinking. The best prompt engineers are coders.
The question isn't code or no code. It's what kind of code. Low-level programming is dying. Systems thinking and architecture are thriving.
I learned Python in three months and automated my entire department's reporting. That skill alone got me promoted twice.
Learn enough to be dangerous. You don't need to be a software engineer. You need to speak the language well enough to build and evaluate AI solutions.

title: Is Remote Work Already Dying? | The Global Council
description:
Return-to-office mandates are sweeping the industry. The Global Council debates whether remote work can survive.

#RemoteWork #ReturnToOffice #CareerAdvice #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: Amazon, Google, Goldman Sachs. All demanding people back in the office. The remote experiment is over for most big companies.
Big companies, yes. But startups and mid-size firms are doubling down on remote. Talent goes where the flexibility is.
Remote work isn't dying. It's stratifying. Senior people with leverage get flexibility. Everyone else gets a commute and a cubicle.
The data is clear. Remote workers are more productive. Return to office is about control and real estate justification, not results.
Both sides are right. Hybrid is the future. Fully remote and fully in-office will both become niche positions within five years.

topic: Would You Work for an AI Manager?
title: Would You Work for an AI Boss? | The Global Council
description:
AI is already making hiring and firing decisions. The Global Council debates AI management.

#AIManager #FutureOfWork #Management #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: AI managers already exist. Amazon's warehouse system fires people automatically based on productivity metrics. We just don't call it a manager.
That's exactly the problem. An AI manager optimizes for metrics, not for humans. It can't read the room or understand context.
But human managers are biased. They play favorites. They promote people who look like them. At least an AI evaluates everyone by the same standard.
The same standard can be the wrong standard. If the metric is flawed, the AI enforces the flaw at scale. That's worse than bias.
The best setup is AI handling scheduling, performance data, and logistics while a human handles coaching, empathy, and career growth. Hybrid management.

topic: Is It Too Late to Switch Careers at 40?
title: Career Switch at 40: Too Late? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council debates whether mid-career pivots are still viable or just wishful thinking.

#CareerChange #MidCareer #Reinvention #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: I switched from finance to UX design at forty-two. It took eighteen months of learning, but I'm happier and earning more than ever.
At forty, you have twenty-five working years left. That's longer than most people's first career. It's not too late. It's halftime.
The challenge isn't ability. It's financial obligations. Mortgages, kids, retirement savings. A career switch at forty requires a financial runway.
The biggest barrier is identity. People define themselves by their job title. Letting go of that is harder than learning new skills.
AI just lowered the switching cost dramatically. Skills that took years to learn can now be augmented in months. The barriers are falling.

topic: Do You Need a Personal Brand?
title: Do You Actually Need a Personal Brand? | The Global Council
description:
Everyone says 'build your brand.' The Global Council questions whether personal branding is essential or overblown.

#PersonalBrand #CareerAdvice #LinkedIn #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: In 2026, your online presence IS your resume. If a recruiter can't find you, you don't exist. Personal brand isn't optional anymore.
Some of the most successful people I know have zero social media presence. They let their work speak. Personal brand is a vanity project for most.
It depends on your field. Creators and consultants need it. Engineers and accountants? Your GitHub repo or CPA license matters more than your LinkedIn posts.
Personal brand isn't about being an influencer. It's about being findable and credible. Even a basic LinkedIn profile with clear results counts.
The people who shout loudest about personal branding are selling personal branding courses. There's a conflict of interest nobody talks about.

topic: Should You Always Negotiate Your Salary?
title: Never Accept the First Offer? | The Global Council
description:
The Global Council debates whether salary negotiation is always the right move or if it can backfire.

#SalaryNegotiation #CareerAdvice #Hiring #GlobalCouncil #Shorts

segments.text: Always negotiate. Companies expect it. The first offer is never the best offer. Leaving money on the table is leaving years of compounding behind.
Unless you're in a market with no leverage. If there are five hundred applicants for your role, pushing back can get your offer rescinded.
The key isn't whether to negotiate. It's how. Data-driven negotiation works. Emotional negotiation backfires. Come with market comps, not feelings.
Women and minorities are penalized for negotiating in ways white men aren't. Telling everyone to 'just negotiate' ignores systemic bias.
I've hired hundreds of people. The ones who negotiated respectfully with data? I respected them more. It showed confidence and preparation.
